artifacts.summary: Confirms Defects 1-3 verbatim against the live source store, finds that lifecycle-notify.sh's 'orchestrate-active' marker has no writer anywhere (dead), that orchestrator-postflight.sh and skill_lifecycle_notify are orphaned for core task types, flags that no existing check or test covers any of the three hook scripts, and designs the Stop-branch utterance, cooldown, and matcher-parity-check fixes for planning.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system source store, scripts/orchestrator-postflight.sh and skill-base.sh's skill_lifecycle_notify function are confirmed orphaned for core task types (general/meta/markdown): those task types route directly to agents from skill-orchestrate, bypassing the lifecycle-skill layer (skill-nix-research etc.) that is the only live caller of skill_lifecycle_notify. Only extension task types with their own dedicated lifecycle SKILL.md files reach lifecycle-notify.sh's TTS path at all today.

lifecycle-notify.sh's .claude/tmp/orchestrate-active marker (checked at its line ~56 to auto-suppress TTS mid-orchestrate) has zero writers anywhere in the agent-system source store or deployed tree -- it is dead code, distinct from the genuinely live workflow-active-<CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID> marker that update-task-status.sh preflight writes and claude-stop-notify.sh/wezterm-preflight-status.sh actually read/clear. The two markers have similar names but must not be conflated when reading or rewording this file's header.

hooks/memory-nudge.sh is the one existing Stop-hook sibling with a working cooldown pattern in this codebase: a plain timestamp file (specs/tmp/memory-nudge-last) compared via NOW-LAST_TIME against a threshold, with mkdir -p before the write. No existing hook keys a cooldown by WEZTERM_PANE, but this timestamp-comparison shape is the directly transferable template for a pane-keyed cooldown elsewhere in the hook family.
